metadata.title: Integrating Software Applications with the Epic Electronic Health Record System
metadata.description: A practitioner's roadmap to mastering Epic EHR integration — from foundational interoperability concepts through advanced API patterns, App Orchard distribution, clinical workflow embedding, and production operations.

sections.title: Healthcare Foundations
sections.description: Core knowledge about EHR systems, healthcare regulations, and clinical terminology that every Epic integration developer must understand before writing code.

sections.title: Core Standards and Security
sections.description: Deep mastery of the FHIR R4 data model and OAuth 2.0 security framework that underpins all Epic API access.

sections.title: Application Development and Interfaces
sections.description: Building SMART on FHIR apps, working with HL7v2 interfaces, and developing against Epic's integration surfaces.

sections.title: Advanced Integration Patterns
sections.description: CDS Hooks, Epic proprietary APIs, bulk data extraction, and clinical workflow embedding for deep EHR integration.

sections.title: Distribution and Operations
sections.description: Getting your app listed on Epic Showroom, managing multi-tenant deployments, and running reliably in production.

sections.title: Architecture and Mastery
sections.description: Capstone integration architecture design, migration planning, reference architectures, and long-term technology strategy.

nodes.title: EHR Systems and Clinical Data Concepts
nodes.description: Understanding Electronic Health Records, clinical data types (demographics, ADT events, orders, results, medications, diagnoses), and the clinical workflows that generate data.

resources.title: Introduction to HL7 FHIR — Dr. Chris Paton (YouTube)
AMA Journal of Ethics — Development of Electronic Health Record

nodes.title: Healthcare Data Exchange History and Standards Landscape
nodes.description: The evolution from HL7v2 through CDA to FHIR, key standards organizations (HL7, IHE, ONC, SMART Health IT), regulatory drivers (HIPAA, HITECH, Cures Act), and interoperability levels.

nodes.title: Epic Integration Surfaces Overview
nodes.description: Comprehensive map of every way software can connect to Epic: FHIR R4 APIs, SMART on FHIR, CDS Hooks, HL7v2 Bridges, Care Everywhere, MyChart, Bulk FHIR, Interconnect, and App Orchard/Showroom.

nodes.title: HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules
nodes.description: HIPAA Privacy Rule (PHI, minimum necessary standard), Security Rule (administrative, physical, technical safeguards), and Breach Notification Rule. The regulatory foundation for all healthcare software.

resources.title: HHS HIPAA for Professionals — Security Rule

nodes.title: Business Associate Agreements and Chain of Trust
nodes.description: BAA requirements, the chain of trust from covered entity through business associates to subcontractors, and vendor relationship management.

nodes.title: 21st Century Cures Act and Information Blocking
nodes.description: Information blocking rules, eight exceptions, enforcement penalties (up to $1M/violation), ONC certification requirements, and HTI-1/HTI-2 rules.

resources.title: AMA Summary of ONC Final Rule

nodes.title: FDA Software as Medical Device (SaMD)
nodes.description: FDA SaMD classification (Class I/II/III), the four-criteria CDS exclusion test, AI/ML-based SaMD regulation, and Quality Management System requirements.

resources.title: FDA Software as a Medical Device — Global Approach
FDA Clinical Decision Support Software Guidance

nodes.title: Clinical Terminology Systems
nodes.description: SNOMED CT, ICD-10-CM/PCS, LOINC, RxNorm, CPT, CVX, and NDC — their structure, use cases, and how they appear in Epic's data.

resources.title: NLM Health Data Standards and Terminologies Tutorial
LOINC Official Website and Search Tool

nodes.title: FHIR Terminology Services and CodeableConcept
nodes.description: FHIR CodeSystem, ValueSet, ConceptMap resources and operations ($lookup, $validate-code, $expand, $translate, $subsumes). The CodeableConcept data type.

nodes.title: FHIR Resource Model and Data Types
nodes.description: The ~150 FHIR resource types, primitive and complex data types (HumanName, CodeableConcept, Reference, Identifier), extensions, contained resources, and serialization formats.

resources.title: Health Informatics on FHIR — Georgia Tech (edX)
Principles of Health Interoperability — Tim Benson (Springer)
Smile Digital Health — FHIR Essentials Guide

nodes.title: FHIR RESTful API Interactions
nodes.description: CRUD operations (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), instance/type/system-level interactions, versioning, conditional operations, and Bundle transactions/batches.

nodes.title: FHIR Search Mastery
nodes.description: Search parameter types, prefixes, modifiers (:exact, :contains, :missing), chaining, reverse chaining, _include/_revinclude, pagination, and result parameters.

nodes.title: US Core Profiles and USCDI
nodes.description: HL7 US Core Implementation Guide, Must Support obligations, USCDI data classes and versions, and how US Core profiles constrain FHIR R4 for US healthcare.

nodes.title: Epic FHIR Implementation
nodes.description: Epic's FHIR R4 support: available resources, operations, write-back capabilities, rate limits, CapabilityStatement, sandbox vs production differences, and Epic-specific extensions.

resources.title: Epic on FHIR Sandbox — Test Environment

nodes.title: FHIR Client Libraries
nodes.description: Client libraries for FHIR development: client-js (JavaScript), fhirclient (Python), HAPI FHIR (Java), Firely SDK (.NET), and FHIRPath expression language.

nodes.title: OAuth 2.0 Core Framework
nodes.description: RFC 6749 fundamentals: authorization code flow, client credentials, roles (resource owner, client, authorization server, resource server), access and refresh tokens, bearer tokens.

nodes.title: PKCE and Modern OAuth Security
nodes.description: Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636): code_verifier, code_challenge, S256 method. CSRF protection, TLS requirements, and why PKCE is mandatory for SMART apps.

resources.title: Auth0 — Authorization Code Flow with PKCE

nodes.title: SMART on FHIR Authorization
nodes.description: SMART App Launch IG v2: FHIR-aware scopes (patient/, user/, system/), launch context, .well-known/smart-configuration discovery, OpenID Connect and fhirUser claim.

resources.title: Health Data Sharing — OAuth, SMART on FHIR (ONC YouTube)
HL7 SMART App Launch IG v2

nodes.title: JWT Backend Service Authentication
nodes.description: Client credentials grant with JWT assertions (RFC 7523): building JWTs with correct claims (iss, sub, aud, jti, exp), RS384 signing, and system-level scopes for unattended access.

resources.title: Building Backend OAuth 2.0 for JWT Assertions (Medium)

nodes.title: JWKS and Key Management
nodes.description: JSON Web Key Sets (RFC 7517): JWKS URL vs static upload, key rotation strategies, kid matching, HSM/vault storage, and production-grade key lifecycle management.

resources.title: Auth0 — JSON Web Key Set Guide

nodes.title: SMART App Launch Framework

SMART on FHIR Tutorial (YouTube — Grahame Grieve)

nodes.title: EHR Launch and Standalone Launch Flows
nodes.description: Two SMART launch modes: EHR Launch (app launched from within Epic, receives opaque launch parameter) and Standalone Launch (app initiates independently, requests context via scopes).

Epic on FHIR Developer Portal / Sandbox
Building SMART on FHIR Apps with MeldRx (YouTube)

nodes.title: SMART Scopes and Permissions

resources.title: SMART Scopes and Launch Context — HL7 IG
Epic on FHIR — Supported SMART Scopes

nodes.title: Embedded Rendering in Hyperspace and MyChart
nodes.description: Rendering SMART apps inside Hyperspace/Hyperdrive iframes and MyChart web/mobile environments. Cross-origin restrictions, responsive design, and viewport handling.

nodes.title: HL7v2 Message Structure and Segments

resources.title: HL7 V2.x: The Developer's Complete Guide (YouTube)

nodes.title: ADT, ORM, ORU, SIU, and MDM Message Types
nodes.description: The five core HL7v2 message types for Epic integration: ADT (patient movement), ORM (orders), ORU (results), SIU (scheduling), and MDM (documents) with their trigger events.

resources.title: Smile Digital Health — HL7 V2 Walkthrough

nodes.title: MLLP Transport and ACK/NAK Patterns
nodes.description: Minimal Lower Layer Protocol for HL7v2 over TCP: framing characters (SB/EB/CR), acknowledgment modes (original/enhanced), AA/AE/AR codes, retry strategies, and error handling.

resources.title: Integrating with Epic using HL7 v2 (YouTube)

nodes.title: Card Response Types and Prefetch
